templates.why_chosen: Textbook three-tier stack in tikz: outer tier containers, inner module rows, and a dashed line naming a trust/network boundary.
templates.what_to_learn: Name tiers in the left margin, keep every module row the same height, and use a single dashed horizontal rule (labelled 'Internet') for the boundary that matters.

templates.why_chosen: High-confidence nested-stack exemplar also cited as the layered template's own gutter exemplar: the LLM Service nests a Manager box that nests four analysis sub-modules, and the LLM Engine nests two modules behind a stacked-instance icon.
templates.what_to_learn: Put the tier name in a left gutter even while nesting sub-boxes inside it, and mark a box that stands for many running copies with a stacked-rectangle offset icon behind it rather than drawing every instance, keeping that as the one extra property at that nesting level.

templates.why_chosen: Replication confined to exactly one tier, as the template recommends: only the bottom-most Parrot LLM Engine box carries a stacked-shadow icon for multiple backend instances, while the four layers above it stay singular.
templates.what_to_learn: Keep replication confined to exactly one tier of a layered stack, here the bottom engine, by giving only that box a stacked-shadow icon; leave every tier above it as a single box so the figure still reads as one layered system, not N whole systems.
